headline: PENTAGON-BACKED $375M RARE EARTH PLANT SET FOR ROCHESTER — Freedom Separation to Process 18,000 Tons/Yr RE Material by 2028
snippet: Phoenix Tailings announced a $375 million commercial-scale rare earth separation facility — the 'Freedom Separation' plant — at Rochester's Eastman Business Park, backed by a conditional $500 million Pentagon debt commitment and $3 million in New York State performance-based tax credits. The 500,000 sq ft facility is part of Phoenix Tailings' $1.2 billion Freedom Project, targeting 4,400+ tonnes per year of separated rare earth oxides at full capacity in 2028 and supporting 200 direct jobs; partial operations are expected to begin in 2027.

headline: K2 GOLD DRAGONFLY HITS 83.82M AT 3.40 G/T — 19.81m Core at 7.51 G/T; 27 Holes Pending at Newmont Zone
snippet: K2 Gold (TSX-V: KTO) released the strongest intercepts of its 2026 program at the Dragonfly gold project in California: 83.82 metres grading 3.40 g/t gold with a high-grade core of 19.81 metres at 7.51 g/t. These are the final four holes from Phase 1; drilling is now underway at the Newmont Zone with assays from 27 additional holes pending in coming weeks, setting up a potential sustained run of results at one of the TSX-V's most closely watched early-stage gold discoveries.

headline: GOLD SLIPS TO $4,124 FOR THIRD SESSION — Oil Spike Revives Fed Rate-Hike Bets Ahead of Oct 27 FOMC
snippet: Physical gold slipped to $4,124 on October 20 — its third consecutive down session — as Brent crude holding near five-month highs amplified Treasury yield pressure and renewed market pricing for a Federal Reserve rate hike at the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. Silver firmed slightly to $57.50 (+0.67%), diverging from gold on the day; the precious metals complex is navigating an unusual macro backdrop where oil-driven inflation and safe-haven demand pull in opposite directions heading into the final week of October.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING APOLLO EXPANDS THREE DIRECTIONS — 560.05m at 1.83 G/T AuEq Confirms Bulk-Tonnage Scale at Colombia Porphyry
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) released drill results expanding the Apollo copper-gold porphyry in three separate directions at its Guayabales project in Colombia, headlined by 560.05 metres grading 1.83 g/t gold equivalent confirming broad continuity across the system. Apollo begins at surface, is mineralized over 1,200 vertical metres, and remains open at depth; drill intercepts also identified a shallow tungsten zone averaging 0.25% WO3, adding polymetallic optionality to one of the TSX's premier porphyry-scale discoveries.

headline: SILVER WORST WEEK IN 2026: DOWN 6.43% — Buenaventura Cuts Output; Gold Miners Amplify Bullion's Decline 2-5x
snippet: Frank Holmes' weekly GoldSeek SWOT survey recorded silver as 2026's worst weekly performer, down 6.43% for the week ending October 17, while GDX and gold equities broadly amplified bullion's pullback two-to-five times. Notable sector developments: Peru's Buenaventura (NYSE: BVN) lowered its full-year direct gold production forecast to 112,000–131,000 ounces — a bellwether for mid-tier producers navigating rising royalty costs — while SSR Mining agreed to acquire Roxmore Resources for approximately $712 million in a Marigold-adjacent Nevada gold consolidation.

headline: AURUM BOUNDIALI HITS 57M AT 2.34 G/T GOLD — 2m Bonanza Core at 37.95 G/T as 3.22 Moz West Africa Resource Update Due End October
snippet: Aurum Resources (ASX: AUE) released 25 diamond drill hole results across three deposit zones at its Boundiali Gold Project in Côte d'Ivoire, with hole BSDD0180 returning 57 metres at 2.34 g/t gold from 290 metres depth including a 2-metre high-grade core at 37.95 g/t. The results precede an updated Mineral Resource Estimate targeted for release before end of October 2026; the project currently carries a 3.22-million-ounce resource and is the focus of a 150,000-metre 2026 campaign aimed at growing ounces at depth and along strike.

headline: McFARLANE LAKE LAUNCHES FULLY FUNDED 50,000M JUBY DRILL PROGRAM — Ontario 1.07 Moz Gold Project Gets Phase 2 Expansion
snippet: McFarlane Lake Mining (TSX-V) outlined a fully funded 50,000-metre Phase 2 drilling program at its Juby Gold Project in Ontario, building on an NI 43-101 estimate of 1.07 million ounces of gold in the Indicated category at 0.96 g/t. The Phase 2 program targets resource expansion beyond the current model at one of Northern Ontario's underexplored Archean greenstone gold systems, with funding confirmed in advance — removing the capital-raise uncertainty that typically delays junior drill programs heading into the winter season.

headline: METALSHUB ADDS LIVE LITHIUM TRADING IN NOVEMBER — Carbonate and Spodumene Join Platform Near Chinese 10-Month Price Low
snippet: Digital metals trading platform Metalshub will launch live trading in battery-grade lithium carbonate, technical-grade lithium carbonate, and spodumene concentrate in November 2026, extending institutional-grade price transparency to a market that has historically relied on bilateral negotiations. The launch arrives as Chinese lithium carbonate prices sit near a 10-month low after retreating approximately 50% from the May 2026 high of 209,880 yuan per tonne, a backdrop that may accelerate consolidation among spot buyers seeking transparent benchmarks.

headline: SOUTH AFRICA HALEU JV SIGNED AT PELINDABA — TerraPower Offtake in Place as QLE-Necsa Commercial Plant Advances
snippet: Quantum Leap Energy (QLE), a subsidiary of ASP Isotopes (NASDAQ: ASPI), signed a binding heads of agreement with South Africa's state-owned Necsa to form an 80/20 joint venture for commercial-scale HALEU (high-assay low-enriched uranium) production at the Pelindaba nuclear site, with an existing TerraPower offtake arrangement in place. A test bench is already built at Pelindaba and building renovations are underway; the deal advances one of the very few non-Russian HALEU supply chains ahead of the first commercial deployments of advanced small modular reactors.

headline: DEEP YELLOW SCRAPS Q4 TUMAS FID — Shares -58% YTD as Western Equity Markets Stall Namibia Uranium; CNNC-Backed Rival Advances
snippet: Deep Yellow (ASX: DYL) abandoned its Q4 2026 final investment decision target for the Tumas uranium project in Namibia — citing weak equity markets — with no new timeline announced; shares have fallen approximately 58% year-to-date. The deferral stands in stark contrast to rival Bannerman Energy, which closed its US$321.5 million strategic financing from CNNC's offshore arm and launched an A$124 million placement targeting its own Q4 2026 FID at the adjacent Etango deposit — illustrating a widening gap between Chinese-backed and Western-equity-dependent uranium developers.
